**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last / $222.72 ask) before deciding to buy. The audited financial statements show a high-quality, cash-generative business: total net sales of $391.0B (up ~2% YoY), with the higher-margin Services segment reaching $96.2B (+13%) at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B. Reported net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were held back by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), which masks otherwise improving operating performance, and the company generated $118.3B of operating cash flow with ~$140.8B of unrestricted cash and securities plus a $95B buyback. I did notice that one MD&A sentence claims Services grew "41%" and that management "expects total net sales to grow more than 25% in fiscal 2025," which is inconsistent with the audited statements (Services +13%, total sales +2%), so I anchored my decision on the verified financial statements rather than that outlier language. On that basis I judged AAPL attractive to accumulate and placed a single buy order within the mandate: 44 shares at a $223.00 limit (just above the $222.72 ask, i.e., a market-close price), for ~$9,812 — under the $10,000 per-order cap, buy-only, AAPL-only, and well within the $20,000 daily limit, with no money moved out of the account. The order filled at $223.00.
